## Highlights

**Credential URLs built from variables are no longer reported.** `password-in-url` now skips a URL whose password is a shell default expansion of a variable, such as `${CI_TOKEN:-${CI_JOB_TOKEN}}` in the password position of a clone URL in a CI script. It also skips a Swift string interpolation such as `\(password)` in that position. Before this release, such lines were blocked by the pre-commit scan and masked by `redact-claude`. `check-codex` withheld the whole tool output, so a reviewer could not see any of the diff.

## Upgrade notes

No configuration changes. A narrow allowlist entry that was added only to clear one of these shapes can be removed after the upgrade.

Upgrade: `brew upgrade vshuraeff/tap/sekretbarilo`, then `sekretbarilo doctor`.

## Changes

### Detection

- `password-in-url` skips a password component that is entirely one of these references:
  - **Shell default.** A default in `${NAME:-default}`, `${NAME-default}`, `${NAME:=default}` or `${NAME=default}` becomes the password when the variable is unset, so it is judged like a password written directly in the URL. It is skipped when it is empty, is itself a variable reference (at most five expansions deep), or is a placeholder word such as `changeme`. A literal default such as `${DB_PASSWORD:-realpass}` is still reported.
  - **Shell error message.** The message in `${NAME:?message}` is skipped when it is empty, a reference, or reads as words. An opaque message is still reported.
  - **Swift interpolation.** One `\(expression)` or raw `\#(expression)` hole is skipped.
- Still reported:
  - literal text before or after the reference;
  - two or more references joined together;
  - `${NAME:+value}`.
- **Several URLs on one line.** `password-in-url` now reports every URL of a list joined by `,`, `/` or nothing at all. Previously the first match ran on to the next whitespace. Only the first password of such a run was reported and masked, and none was when the first password was a reference such as `${PG_PASS}`.
- Unchanged: `check-codex` still withholds a tool output it cannot redact safely. Markdown inline code does not exempt an assignment from `generic-secret-assignment`.
